title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR free/voluntary imputation; PLAC needs Scripture
pass_a_gloss: GAR's sure line: first-sin imputation is God's free, willing act from settled counsel and judgment, not nature's order alone. No counselor of God is bound to know or explain what God left unsaid in Scripture. Enough that we know the fact—all sinned in Adam, guilt reached all for condemnation, so the first sin comes down on all by imputation. Reasons of that judgment rest with God; His paths cannot be traced and His judgments are a deep gulf (Romans 11:33; Psalm 36:7). PLAC: A free, willing divine act of immediate first-sin imputation is unknowable unless Scripture discloses it. Scripture does not; and the texts he recycles here do not prove it—as partly shown already, and as more will show.
pass_b_english: GAR. We have a sure reply ready: that the imputation of the first sin is a free and voluntary action of God, from God's fixed counsel and judgment, not depending on the order of nature alone. And that no one was God's counselor, bound to know those things and to answer concerning them which God refused to reveal in His word. That it is enough for us to know the thing itself—namely that all sinned in Adam, and his guilt came upon all unto condemnation, and so that first sin descends upon all by imputation. That the reasons of that judgment are with God, whose ways are unsearchable, and His judgments a great deep. Romans 11:33. Psalm 36:7. PLAC. If the immediate imputation of the first sin is a free and voluntary action of God, it cannot be known unless it has been revealed in Scripture. But it is not revealed in Scripture, nor do the places repeated here by the learned man have any force to prove it, as has partly already appeared, and will partly be made plain from what is to be said.
source_text: GAR. Nobis certa responsio suppetit, imputationem primi peccati esse actionem Dei liberam & voluntariam, ex certo Dei consilio judicioque, non ex solius naturae ordine dependentem. Neminem autem fuisse Dei consiliarium, qui ea nosse, & de iis respondere teneatur, quae Deus in verbo suo revelare noluit. Sufficere nobis ipsius rei notitiam, omnes scilicet in Adamo peccasse, & ipsius reatum super omnes venisse in condemnationem, atque ita primum illud peccatum in omnes imputatione descendere. Rationes illius judicii penes Deum esse cujus viae sunt impervestigabiles, & eius judicia abyssus multa. Rom. xi. 33. Psalm. xxxvi. 7. PLAC. Si immediata imputatio primi peccati est actio Dei libera & voluntaria, ea nisi in Scriptura revelata fuerit, sciri non potest. Atqui non est in Scriptura revelata, neque ad eam probandam ullam vim habent loca a viro docto hic repetita, ut partim jam patuit, partim ex dicendis manifestum fiet.
